name: Blush Figma asset plugin successor
demand: Blush had 446,248 reported installs; Dev Resources says its latest published version was July 28, 2021, based on a Figma Community check on September 15, 2026. A separate tracker reported 666,987 users and 446,845 saves on October 13, 2026; those are third-party metrics, not verified active or paying users. Figma’s S-1 reports over 13 million monthly active users in Q1 2025, about two-thirds of them non-designers; this is a platform audience, not the addressable market for illustration plugins. Search volume and a relevant regulated population: unverified/not applicable. Sources: https://devresourc.es/blog/best-figma-plugins ; https://fig-stats.com/plugins/838959511417581040 ; https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0001579878/4861e748-6e2b-43d4-874d-b7ef6e7a262f.pdf
prices: Blush: current exact price unverified; secondary pages checked in October 2026 report $12/month billed annually, $15/month billed quarterly, or $20 monthly, while another directory says the maker does not publish prices. GetIllustrations: $195 for one year of illustration access, $249 for one year of Ultimate access with two team seats, or $99 quarterly. Illustro: $7, $15, or $45 one-time credit packs. Storyset: free illustrations require attribution; its FAQ says a Flaticon Premium subscription removes attribution. Sources: https://yespress.io/blush ; https://www.thegeeksclub.com/platforms/blush/pricing/ ; https://techyorker.com/products/blush/ ; https://getillustrations.com/pricing/all-options ; https://illustro.app/pricing ; https://storyset.com/faqs
copy_speed: The cheap survive verdict needs revisiting: Illustro announced its Figma Marketplace plugin on June 29, 2026; it puts generated illustrations into Figma and sells credit packs. Kitbitz was announced on August 19, 2026 with a Figma plugin and 2,000+ free CC0 illustrations. These are two recent direct or adjacent substitutes, one paid and one free; neither source proves sales or revenue. Sources: https://illustro.app/blog/illustro-on-figma-marketplace ; https://illustro.app/pricing ; https://www.reddit.com/r/FigmaDesign/comments/1vsivil/i_made_over_2000_handdrawn_illustrations_in_figma/ ; https://kitbitz.art/
platform_risk: High distribution dependence on Figma: plugins require review, updates can be reviewed, and Figma reserves discretion to reject plugins; it permits third-party monetization subject to its rules. Plugins must be manually run, one at a time, and cannot act in the background. Paid functionality should use a classic plugin: Figma says monetization is unsupported for generative plugins. Figma is also adding native drawing and vector tools. Sources: https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039958914-Plugin-and-widget-review-guidelines ; https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042532714-Use-plugins-in-files ; https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/41407987481879-About-building-plugins-in-Figma ; https://www.figma.com/blog/introducing-vectorize/
defensible_asset: No strong moat is evident in the lead as stated. Inserted SVGs are portable; a defensible version would need independently commissioned or exclusively licensed, coherent collections plus useful team presets and saved styles, which could create modest workflow switching costs. There is no evident UK-specific data or rules engine. Do not build from Blush’s library: its license says the illustrations cannot be redistributed or compiled into a competing service. Sources: https://blush.design/license ; https://agentgid.com/assets/blush/ ; https://illustratorsaustralia.com/resources/commissioning-guidelines
build_effort: Technical MVP is a classic JavaScript/HTML Figma plugin with a hosted catalog, search, insertion, accounts, entitlements, and billing; Figma documents the Plugin API and external network requests. Calendar effort is unverified. The harder ongoing work is sourcing and clearing rights, art direction, quality review, and support. AI agents could handle asset tagging/search assistance, routine support triage, billing workflows, and release monitoring; human approval of artwork, rights, and plugin quality remains necessary. Sources: https://developers.figma.com/docs/plugins/ ; https://developers.figma.com/docs/plugins/making-network-requests/ ; https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039958914-Plugin-and-widget-review-guidelines
channel: Use inbound Figma Community discovery, a branded product page, and search-led content; test with public community posts rather than unsolicited messages. Collect email only through explicit opt-in. ICO guidance says unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals, including sole traders, generally needs consent; electronic mail includes social direct messages. Sources: https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042532714-Use-plugins-in-files ; https://forum.figma.com/showcase-your-work-14/svgenius-ai-svg-illustration-generator-for-figma-51177 ; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/how-do-we-comply-with-the-pecr-electronic-mail-marketing-rules/
owner_hours_per_week: ≤5 hours is an unverified steady-state target, plausible only with a stable catalog, self-serve billing, and automated routine support. Asset rights, curation, quality control, launch, and early support may exceed it.
desk_test: Within one day, first install Blush and test its current Figma workflow and paid path; the 2021 plugin-version date alone does not establish that the product is broken. Then make a small clickable catalog/team-license mockup and a branded page showing one explicit proposed price, with a refundable preorder. Share it in a relevant public design community and count only a completed payment from outside the founder’s network as positive evidence; likes and email signups alone do not validate payment. Proposed price and pass criterion are experiment settings, not market facts. Sources: https://devresourc.es/blog/best-figma-plugins ; https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500002628062-Comments-on-Community
red_flags: No lead-specific revenue, paid-user count, or recent complaint evidence verified. Installs and listed competitor prices do not prove Blush has paying users. Current Blush plugin functionality remains unverified, so age of its last reported version is not proof of abandonment. Two recent substitutes were found, including free CC0 assets; the generic successor has weak defensibility. The ≤5 hours/week and 55% automation figures are operating hypotheses, not measured results. I would kill the generic version unless the desk test validates paid demand for a distinct, rights-cleared library and team workflow.
